$comment: Canonical shape of Shared/data's offline Today datasets. The files are generated in Shared and physically copied into all three apps. The selected calendar controls both its feast file and readingsFile. Missing data hides the corresponding row; it never falls back to another rite. See ../ARCHITECTURE.markdown#offline-today-data-shareddata.

default.description: Calendar id used when feastCalendarId is absent or unknown.

file.description: Basename of this calendar's feast JSON.

readingsFile.description: Basename of this calendar's citation JSON. LPJ and General Roman intentionally share readings-roman.

paschaVariants.description: Optional matched feast and reading tables. The easternPaschaStyle preference selects both together; absent/unknown values use defaultPaschaStyle.

calendarRegistry.legacyMigration: Persisted roman-he maps to roman; roman-he is not a selectable calendar and has no dataset.

feastDataset.files: Feast files named by CalendarDefinition.file and each paschaVariants entry

rank.description: Canonical rank used by calendar logic and title prominence. Localize its display caption using the Today language without changing this value.

titleByLanguage.description: All six non-English interface locales are populated for shipped dates. Sourced identities take precedence over credited editorial display metadata; reviewed aliases never change dates, ranks or observances. Hebrew Pentecost uses שבועות. Future unsupported labels fall back to the source title.

readings.description: Ordered appointed citations only; no Scripture text.

ReadingCitation.constraints: Every numeric range uses an en dash. Hebrew short/full values use book + gematria chapter + Arabic verse numbers with no colon. Arabic full citations use LRI/PDI around the numeric reference to preserve range order in RTL.

short.description: Compact home form, normally book plus chapter.

full.description: Complete book/chapter/verse citation shown after expansion.

hebrew.description: Legacy full Hebrew citation accepted by readers; new generators write fullByLanguage.he.

sources.readings-roman: Evangelizo publication edition HE (Novus Ordo; includes sourced Hebrew citation maps)
sources.readings-roman1962: Missale Meum public proper API (Vetus Ordo)
sources.readings-ugcc: UGCC Patriarchal Liturgical Commission official 2026 calendar; Ukraine new-style fixed feasts and Julian Pascha
sources.readings-ugcc-gregorian: Royal Doors public UGCC fully Gregorian calendar

languagePreference.description: Today always follows the app/interface language, independently of defaultLanguageCode. There is no Today language picker. Previously persisted todayLanguageCode is ignored. iw and fil normalize to he and tl; Arabic and Hebrew apply RTL to the complete Today stack, including expanded citations.

intentionDataset.fallback: Missing language uses published English; missing month hides the row. Hebrew is credited to Prosary, not to an official Vatican Hebrew edition.

torahDataset.source: Hebcal.com, CC BY 4.0, Eretz Israel only (i=on)
torahDataset.selection: The selected civil day maps to the next Saturday, including Saturday itself. A holiday Torah service replaces the weekly portion; diaspora schedules are never requested. Only books of the Torah are included, without haftarah or festival megillot.
torahDataset.language: Source Hebrew, French and Russian proper names where supplied by Hebcal; source transliterations for remaining locales, with localized interface captions and citation book names.

dateNavigation.state: Local civil selected date, initially today; independent of prayer progress and prayer-day computation.
dateNavigation.controls: Previous day arrow, centered formatted-date button, next day arrow. Date button opens a native calendar with a Today action inside its popup.
dateNavigation.supplementalDayRow: Hidden on every Sunday. On weekdays, lpj/roman use the modern Roman seasonal day; roman1962 and all Eastern calendars show the localized civil day and month, never Ordinary Time.
dateNavigation.bounds: Respect each native picker’s supported civil-date range; Android uses 1900–2100. Missing date or month data hides only its corresponding row.
